summary:
Tested new Forward-Test walk-forward engine + MetaApi datasource integration on Apex Flow. 8/8 backend pytest cases pass (datasource/status, forward-test EUR/USD & multi-symbol BTC/USDT + XAU/USD + US30, invalid symbol 404, execute-live disconnected safety, invalid symbol for execute-live). Frontend: demo login works, Forward-Test panel renders full-width, source badge, run button starts replay, live stats (winrate, PnL, equity, trade log), pause/resume/speed 1x/3x/6x/skip all work. AI analysis, backtest, watchlist, positions and existing dashboard features regress-clean.

IMPORTANT DEVIATION FROM REQUEST: The request stated broker is DISCONNECTED and expected source='simulated' + badge 'DATI SIMULATI'. Reality at test time: GET /api/datasource/status returns connected=true, connection_status='CONNECTED' (Tickmill broker IS live), so /forwardtest/run for EUR/USD, XAU/USD, US30 returns source='real' and the UI shows 'TICKMILL CONNESSO' / 'DATI REALI TICKMILL'. Only BTC/USDT falls back to 'simulated' (Tickmill likely lacks that symbol). The graceful-fallback code path is exercised for BTC/USDT and works correctly. execute-live still returns ok=false with error (broker connected but order rejected — expected in DEMO env). Nothing crashes.
action_items: INFO ONLY (not a bug): Broker is now actually CONNECTED. The request expected disconnected/simulated state but MetaApi provisioning API returns CONNECTED for account 85584886-eac6-441c-9641-7e8dff74426a. UI/labels correctly reflect this ('DATI REALI TICKMILL' / 'TICKMILL CONNESSO'). If the user still expects the simulated fallback to be visually demonstrated, they can force it by temporarily unsetting METAAPI_TOKEN or picking a symbol Tickmill doesn't have (e.g. BTC/USDT already falls back).

OBSERVATION: On real Tickmill EUR/USD M15 candles, the walk-forward engine produced 0 trades (winrate stayed 0% even after skip-to-end). The SMC entry rules (order block retest within 0.1% of top/bottom) may be too tight for real market prices. Backend tests still pass because they only require total_trades >= 0. Consider loosening tolerance or extending the fallback FVG retest window if real-data trade generation is desired.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now 710 lines — crossed the 700-line threshold. Recommend splitting into routers (auth.py, market.py, ai.py, bot.py, positions.py, backtest.py, forwardtest.py).
metaapi_service._state is a module-level mutable dict — fine for single-worker uvicorn but would break under multiple workers/replicas. Not a concern in current supervisor setup.
run_forward_test recomputes smart_money_zones on every bar (O(n*warmup)) — for bars=600 this is ~27k swing-point scans. Acceptable for demo but could be memoized/incremental.

In ForwardTest.jsx, res.equity_curve[idx] is accessed without bounds check when idx > len — safe today because setIdx clamps, but a defensive `res.equity_curve[Math.min(idx, res.equity_curve.length-1)] ?? 0` would be safer.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Broker connection state is dynamic; do not hard-assert connected=false. Use `assert d['source'] in ('simulated','real')` and check field presence. BTC/USDT reliably returns 'simulated' (Tickmill missing symbol) so it's a good test-case for exercising the fallback path. Backend tests in /app/backend/tests/test_forwardtest.py are the new regression suite for this feature; run with `pytest backend/tests/test_forwardtest.py`.
rca of the issue: N/A — no functional bugs. The only 'unexpected' observation (broker connected instead of disconnected) is an external state change on the user's side, not an app bug.
